key_insight: TT-SCHA computes binary-alloy crystal free energies without random sampling, matching molecular dynamics within 0.13 meV per atom at 600–1000 K with 420–500× fewer core-seconds per run.
engineering_relevance: The method could lower the computational cost of predicting alloy thermodynamics, thermal expansion, and elastic properties within embedded-atom potential models.
method: Apply a self-consistent harmonic approximation with corrections through third order in temperature.
Evaluate local thermal averages using tensor-train integrals over one atom and its neighbors.
Obtain infinite-crystal results without finite-size sampling or random-sampling error.
evidence_signal: Tests on B2 NiAl and γ-TiAl used 65,536-atom molecular dynamics as a free-energy benchmark; zero-pressure γ-TiAl results also matched published same-potential elastic constants within 1 GPa and thermal expansion within 0.012 percentage points.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two ordered alloys with embedded-atom potentials, and interpolation starting pivots introduce numerical pressure errors up to 9 MPa, reduced by averaging three runs.
paper_title: TT-SCHA for Thermodynamics of Binary Alloys
